records.label: Wolf
records.visual_function: Establish a readable wolf-derived head, silhouette, and species anatomy while leaving character-specific proportions and grooming available for separate identity decisions.
records.prompt: Build the subject from a coherent wolf morphology: a tapered muzzle, alert triangular ears, canid nose structure, balanced cheek planes, and a clearly readable tail and limb language appropriate to the chosen domain.
invariants: the head retains a recognizable canid muzzle and ear relationship
the nose, cheek, jaw, and eye placement read as one coherent species structure
domain adaptation preserves the wolf identity across upright and quadrupedal forms
misreadings_to_avoid: human face with decorative animal ears

records.label: Cat
records.visual_function: Establish a readable felid head, silhouette, and species anatomy while leaving character-specific proportions and grooming available for separate identity decisions.
records.prompt: Build the subject from a coherent felid morphology: a short rounded muzzle, large forward-set eyes, mobile triangular ears with visible inner structure, a compact jaw, and a flexible tail and limb language appropriate to the chosen domain.
invariants: the head retains a recognizable felid muzzle and ear relationship
the eyes, nose, and cheek planes read as one coherent species structure
domain adaptation preserves the cat identity across upright and quadrupedal forms
misreadings_to_avoid: human face with decorative animal ears

records.label: Dragon
records.visual_function: Establish a readable draconic head, silhouette, and creature anatomy while leaving character-specific proportions, surface treatment, and wing presence available for separate identity decisions.
records.prompt: Build the subject from a coherent draconic morphology: an elongated reptilian muzzle, horn or crest structures that follow the skull, a long flexible neck and tail, and a deliberately chosen set of wing, scale and frill features that share one construction.
invariants: the head retains a recognizable reptilian muzzle and crest relationship
the neck, tail, and wing masses share one believable skeletal logic
domain adaptation preserves the dragon identity across upright and quadrupedal forms
misreadings_to_avoid: generic lizard head without draconic structure
decorative horns floating off the skull
wings that attach without shoulder anatomy
